text:
maria: Quick proposal: introduce a 'fence' + 'handshake' flow as an explicit enforcement boundary across hosted/dedicated/private. Idea: fences are immutable capability objects created by control plane; handshakes produce short-lived lease tokens bound to a fence and node identity.

kai: hmm. how is this materially different from our existing manifests or leases?

maria: key differences: (1) fences are immutable enforcement objects (snapshotable for audit); (2) fences explicitly enumerate enforcement primitives (allowed_actions, kv_cache_policy, kms_whitelist, egress_constraints) rather than informal flags scattered in manifests; (3) handshake binds policy to runtime identity/time so enforcement is trustable.

leah: show a tiny example please

maria: example fence YAML sketch:
```
fence:
  id: fence-2026-03-01
  hosting: private
  allowed_actions: [inference, embeddings]
  kv_cache: disabled
  kms_whitelist: [cust-kms-123]
  fallback_policy: degrade
```
controlplane mints handshake token bound to fence id + node cert fingerprint + epoch; runtime accepts lease_id referencing cached fence.

david: latency concern: we can't handshake per request.

maria: agreed — handshake is per-lease. flow: create lease -> complete handshake -> runtime caches fence by lease_id in shared mem. requests carry lease_id only. rotation triggers new handshake.

kai: sounds similar to residency leases. Are we renaming?

maria: overlaps, but fences are purpose-built for enforcement semantics. Residency handled placement/affinity; fences carry explicit gate semantics and fallback mappings.

josh: overflow paths? hosted -> dedicated fallback?

maria: fence includes fallback_policy: {fail_closed, degrade_to: model-variant, proxy_via: gateway}. This makes behavior explicit and auditable.

leah: ops: immutability = good for audits. creation UX?

maria: both API + Console templates. auto-generate fences for common workload profiles to ease onboarding.

ops-bot: note: we'll need a migration shim to synthesize fences from existing manifests during rollout. Ops checklist: backfill fence ids and keep mapping for rollback.

david: runtime changes? small plugin + in-memory lease cache, validate handshake signature + node attestation.

kai: plugin plan: fast lookup table keyed by lease_id in shared memory; enforcement checks: allowed_actions, kv_cache flag, kms whitelist, egress rules. cheap path for hot tokenized requests.

maria: security: handshake tokens must be short TTL + bound to node cert and optional SG attest. replay protection via nonce+epoch.

josh: propose token shape: lease_id|node_fingerprint|iat|exp|sig. validate mtls + signature chain.

leah: migration: compatibility layer accepts old manifest blobs at handshake time and synthesizes equivalent fence objects with best-effort mappings; mark those fences as 'synthesized' for operator visibility.

maria: next steps: 1) RFC draft (problem statement, simple prototype plan), 2) runtime prototype (kai), 3) migration shim + console templates (maria + leah), 4) security review of handshake token (josh).

kai: I can build the runtime prototype (plugin + in-memory cache).

leah: I'll draft the RFC and migration strategy, include audit log format and examples.

josh: I'll draft the token spec and threat model.

maria: I'll do Console UX + template set.

ops-bot: reminder: tag RFC `hosting-abstraction` and set review due in two weeks. :calendar:
